versions.changelog: Which output? disambiguation (levels-chart vs registry), explicit capabilities declaration, BTC candles via CoinGecko, clearer HTML titles. Runtime pinned to openclaw-v0.1.6.
Input formats section with copy-paste examples (VTT command + minimal post source JSON); explicit note that manual caption cleaning is not needed. Runtime pinned to openclaw-v0.1.5.

Quote validation tolerates timestamps and speaker marks; rolling-duplicate verification text; URL fallback source matching; YouTube external_id convention documented. Runtime pinned to git tag openclaw-v0.1.4 (SHA inside the package).
Fix runtime pin verification comment (openclaw-v0.1.3) and replace invalid shell abort with executable rev-parse check; SHA ec77ba6 pinned inside the package.
Runtime pin: full commit SHA now pinned inside the package (openclaw-v0.1.2) with post-clone rev-parse verification; display name fix.

- Removed skill-card.md file.
- Updated SKILL.md to clarify that this is a skills-only ClawHub release and does not include the Python runtime.
- Strengthened instructions that FES_ROOT must point to a separately installed, version-pinned runtime—never infer a bundled runtime/ directory.
- Added checks for network access and source rights in usage modes.
- Explicitly stated limitations on dependency and database setup: require user confirmation and never write inside the skill or runtime directory.
- Added reference to source handling limits and external runtime install link.

Initial release: Index and audit financial experts’ public statements from YouTube and Telegram

- Extracts verbatim, source-backed "call cards" from expert content
- Searches a local SQLite database of indexed financial theses
- Charts recorded price levels against real market prices for comparison
- Supports four modes: ingestion (index new source), search, charting, and setup
- Enforces strict data rules—never invents or fills in missing quotes, sources, or dates
- Designed for transparency and auditability; no investment advice is provided
